q.s: The 'ship seal' of the Harappan civilisation was found at which site?
q.x: The ship seal comes from Lothal, the Harappan dockyard town; cylindrical seals come from Kalibangan and Mohenjodaro.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in present-day India?
q.x: Mohenjodaro is in Larkana, Sindh (Pakistan); Lothal, Kalibangan and Banawali are in India.

q.s: The Harappan port town of Lothal stands on the bank of which river?
q.x: Lothal lies on the Bhogava near the Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT correctly matched with its location?
q.x: Kalibangan is on the Ghaggar in Rajasthan; Lothal is the site near the Gulf of Khambhat.

q.s: The most widely accepted explanation for the decline of the Harappan civilisation is:
o: Climate change and the drying of the Sarasvati
q.x: The decline is now seen as gradual (c. 1900-1700 BCE) and multi-causal, with climate change and the drying of the Sarasvati most widely accepted.

q.s: Who first noticed the kinship of Sanskrit with Latin and Greek, leading to the idea of the Indo-European family?
q.x: Sir William Jones (1786) pointed out the kinship of Sanskrit with Latin and Greek.

q.s: The Dardic branch of the Indo-European languages is associated with which region of India?
q.x: Dardic languages such as Kashmiri belong to Jammu and Kashmir.

q.s: In the Rigvedic age, the intoxicating fermented drink, as distinct from the ritual drink soma, was called:
q.x: Sura was the intoxicating drink, while soma was the ritual drink offered in sacrifices.

q.s: The word 'gotra', which first occurs in the Rigveda, literally means:
q.x: Gotra literally means cow-pen; gotra exogamy later barred marriage within the same gotra.

q.s: Who wrote 'Kinship Organization in India' (1953), dividing India into four kinship zones?
q.x: Irawati Karve's 1953 work divided India into four kinship zones.

q.s: The famous prayer 'Asato ma sadgamaya' occurs in which Upanishad?
q.x: Asato ma sadgamaya is from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad; the Chandogya has the story of Satyakama Jabala.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Upanishad in which it occurs?
q.x: The Shvetashvatara Upanishad introduces bhakti.

q.s: Which of the following schools is NOT correctly matched with its path to liberation?
q.x: Advaita Vedanta seeks liberation through jnana, the knowledge of the identity of Atman and Brahman.

q.s: Which of the following Upanishadic concepts is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
o: Moksha – law of action and consequence
q.x: Moksha is liberation; the law linking action and consequence is Karma.

q.s: Where did the Buddha spend his last rainy season?
q.x: The Buddha spent his last rainy season at Beluva near Vaishali before reaching Kushinagar.

q.s: The four Buddhist councils were held at all of the following places EXCEPT:
q.x: The councils were at Rajgir, Vaishali, Pataliputra and Kashmir.

q.s: Siddhartha's leaving home at the age of 29 is known in Buddhist tradition as:
q.x: The Great Renunciation is the Mahabhinishkramana, prompted by the four sights.

q.s: What was the name of the horse on which Siddhartha left his palace?
q.x: He left on the horse Kanthaka with the charioteer Channa.

q.s: Makkhali Gosala, founder of the Ajivika sect, was for about six years a companion of:
q.x: Gosala was Mahavira's companion for about six years; the Bhagavati Sutra records their quarrel.

q.s: Which of the following Mauryan finds is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Queen's Edict (on Karuvaki) is on the Allahabad pillar; Junagadh has Rudradaman I's inscription on the Sudarshana lake.

q.s: The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I says the Sudarshana lake was built in Chandragupta Maurya's reign by:
q.x: Governor Pushyagupta built the Sudarshana lake; Tushaspha added canals under Ashoka.

q.s: The Lomas Rishi and Sudama caves of the Mauryan period are located on which hill?
q.x: Lomas Rishi and Sudama are in the Barabar group; Gopika is the largest of the Nagarjuni caves.

q.s: The Prayaga Prashasti of Samudragupta on the Allahabad pillar was composed by:
q.x: The Allahabad Pillar inscription was composed by Harisena; Ravikirti wrote the Aihole inscription.

q.s: The Allahabad pillar carries all of the following inscriptions EXCEPT:
q.x: Rudradaman I's inscription is at Junagadh; the Allahabad pillar was first set up at Kaushambi.

q.s: Which Chola ruler was killed on an elephant at the battle of Koppam (1053)?
q.x: Rajadhiraja I fell at Koppam; Rajendra II was crowned on the battlefield.

q.s: The Chola dynasty came to an end in 1279 when Rajendra III was defeated by:
q.x: The Pandya Maravarman Kulasekara defeated Rajendra III, the last Chola ruler.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a ruler of the Sayyid dynasty?
q.x: Bahlul Lodi founded the Lodi dynasty after the last Sayyid, Alauddin Alam Shah; Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid line.

q.s: Which of the following musical instruments is NOT of Indo-Islamic origin?
q.x: The sarangi is an indigenous Indian bowed instrument; the sitar is cited as the classic Indo-Islamic instrument.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi is correct?
o: It came to an end with Akbar's death
Todar Mal was its only Hindu member
It had a mass following beyond Akbar's court
q.x: Din-i-Ilahi had only about 18 members; Abul Fazl was its chief exponent and Birbal its only Hindu member.

q.s: In 1580, Akbar divided the Mughal empire into how many subas?
q.x: Akbar divided the empire into 12 subas in 1580; the number later rose to 15.

q.s: In the Mughal administration, the kotwal was responsible for:
q.x: The kotwal kept order in towns; villages had the muqaddam, patwari and chowkidar.

q.s: Jagat Gosain, the Rathor wife of Jahangir, was the mother of:
q.x: Jagat Gosain (Jodh Bai) was Shah Jahan's mother.

q.s: Which daughter of Shah Jahan nursed him during his captivity in Agra fort?
q.x: Jahanara, the eldest daughter, supported Dara and nursed the captive Shah Jahan; Roshanara backed Aurangzeb.

q.s: Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of:
q.x: Ibn Battuta came under Muhammad bin Tughluq and served as qazi of Delhi.

q.s: Which of the following foreign visitors is NOT correctly matched with the ruler of his time?
q.x: Domingo Paes visited Vijayanagara under Krishnadeva Raya.

q.s: Jayadeva composed the Gita Govinda at the court of which ruler?
q.x: Jayadeva was a court poet of Lakshmana Sena of Bengal.

q.s: Raskhan, the Muslim devotee who wrote poems on Krishna, was originally named:
q.x: Raskhan's original name was Sayyid Ibrahim.

q.s: Bammera Potana dedicated his Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu to:
q.x: Potana refused the Rachakonda king and dedicated the Bhagavatamu to Lord Rama.

q.s: The titles 'Kavi Brahma' and 'Ubhaya Kavi Mitrudu' belong to which Telugu poet?
q.x: These are Tikkana's titles; Potana was called Sahaja Panditudu.

q.s: Which Sufi order was the chief patron of sama (musical) assemblies?
q.x: The Chishtis patronised sama, which the orthodox Naqshbandis opposed.

q.s: The Lahjat-i-Sikandar Shahi, a Persian work on music drawn from Sanskrit sources, is associated with:
q.x: It is linked with Sikandar Lodi's reign.

q.s: Which Bijapur governor gave Francois Martin the land on which Pondicherry was founded?
q.x: Sher Khan Lodi, Bijapur governor of Valikondapuram, granted the land (1673).

q.s: Mahe, a French settlement acquired in 1725, lies on which coast?
q.x: Mahe is on the Malabar coast in Kerala; Pondicherry and Karaikal are on the Coromandel coast.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the battle of Ambur (1749) is correct?
o: Nawab Anwaruddin was killed in it
It was the last battle of the Third Carnatic War
After it Muhammad Ali became Nawab of the Carnatic
It was fought near Madras in 1757
q.x: Ambur, near Vellore, opened the Second Carnatic War; Anwaruddin was killed, Chanda Sahib became Nawab and Muhammad Ali fled to Trichinopoly.

q.s: In 1758 Col. Forde defeated the French under Conflans in the Andhra region at the battle of:
q.x: At Chandurti (1758) Forde, aided by Ananda Gajapati, defeated Conflans.

q.s: Slavery in India was abolished by Act V of 1843 during the tenure of:
q.x: Act V of 1843 came under Ellenborough.

q.s: Which of the following measures is NOT correctly matched with the Governor-General?
q.x: The Caste Disabilities Removal Act, 1850 came under Dalhousie.

q.s: Who became the first Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act, 1773?
q.x: The Regulating Act made Warren Hastings the first Governor-General of Bengal.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Regulating Act, 1773?
o: A Board of Control was created to supervise the Company
The Bombay and Madras presidencies were subordinated to Bengal
A Supreme Court was set up at Calcutta
The Governor of Bengal became Governor-General of Bengal
q.x: The Board of Control came with Pitt's India Act, 1784.

q.s: Who was the Viceroy of India from 1931 to 1936?
q.x: Willingdon served 1931-36; Irwin was 1926-31 and Linlithgow from 1936.

q.s: Which of the following Viceroys is NOT correctly matched with his tenure?
q.x: Lord Reading was Viceroy in 1921-26.

q.s: The Chapekar brothers shot the plague commissioner Rand at Pune in 1897 during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: The killing of Rand and Ayerst (1897) came under Elgin II, over harsh plague measures.

q.s: The Hilton Young Commission (1926) fixed the exchange rate of the rupee at:
q.x: It fixed 1s 6d; Indian business wanted 1s 4d. Its central-bank recommendation led to the RBI in 1935.

q.s: Under Cornwallis's police arrangement, the rural districts were divided into thanas placed under:
q.x: Rural areas were divided into thanas under darogas, while the kotwal remained chief of town police.

q.s: B.R. Ambedkar's Mahad Satyagraha (1927) was a struggle for the right to:
o: Draw water from the Chavdar tank
q.x: Mahad (1927) was for water from the Chavdar tank; Kalaram (1930) was for temple entry.

q.s: In which year did Ambedkar found the Independent Labour Party?
q.x: The Independent Labour Party was founded in 1936, after the Poona Pact (1932).

q.s: The Telugu poem 'Gabbilam' was written by:
q.x: Gabbilam is Gurram Jashuva's work; Paleru is by Boyi Bhimanna.

q.s: Which of the following Telugu works is NOT correctly matched with its author?
q.x: Nimna Jatula Charitra is by Jala Rangaswamy.

q.s: Which of the following reformers is NOT correctly matched with her work?
o: Savitribai Phule – Home for the Prevention of Infanticide
q.x: Sharada Sadan was founded by Pandita Ramabai; Anandibai Joshi was the first Indian woman with a Western medical degree.

q.s: Ambedkar's Kalaram Temple Satyagraha (1930) was held at:
q.x: The Kalaram temple-entry satyagraha was at Nashik (1930-35).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its year?
q.x: The Independent Labour Party was founded in 1936; the other three are correct.

q.s: Who designed the tricolour flag that Gandhi hoisted at the Bezawada AICC session of 1921?
q.x: Pingali Venkayya of Machilipatnam designed the flag presented at Bezawada (1921).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pingali Venkayya – designed the flag shown at Bezawada (1921)
Ponaka Kanakamma – women's wing at the Kakinada session (1923)
q.x: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular belongs to the Quit India Movement, 1942.

q.s: Who founded the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885 and was known as the 'Lion of Bombay'?
q.x: Pherozeshah Mehta founded it with Telang and Badruddin Tyabji.

q.s: 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas' was written by:
q.x: Tilak wrote it; Lajpat Rai wrote Unhappy India and Pal The Soul of India.

q.s: Which of the following books is NOT correctly matched with its author?
o: The Soul of India – Bipin Chandra Pal
The Arctic Home in the Vedas – Tilak
q.x: Gita Rahasya was written by Tilak.

q.s: The Provisional Government of India at Kabul (December 1915) had as its President:
q.x: Raja Mahendra Pratap was President and Barkatullah Prime Minister.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Indian revolutionaries abroad during the First World War is correct?
o: The Berlin Committee sought the help of Russia and Japan
Amir Habibullah openly helped the Provisional Government
The Provisional Government of India at Kabul was set up in December 1915
The Provisional Government was set up at Berlin
q.x: The Berlin Committee sought German and Turkish help; at Kabul it was crown prince Amanullah, not Amir Habibullah, who helped.

q.s: Who called herself 'an Indian Tom-Tom'?
q.x: Annie Besant described herself as an Indian Tom-Tom, waking those who slept.

q.s: Which of the following quotes is NOT correctly matched with the leader?
o: The British Empire is rotten to the core – Gandhi
I am an Indian Tom-Tom – Annie Besant
First we are Indians, then Muslims – Jinnah
q.x: 'The British Empire is rotten to the core' was said by Sister Nivedita.

q.s: Rajuvula and Sodasa were Shaka satraps of which region?
q.x: They belonged to the Mathura branch; Bhumaka and Nahapana were Kshaharatas of the upper Deccan.

q.s: Lilavati, a Sri Lankan princess, was the queen of which Satavahana king?
q.x: Lilavati was Hala's queen.

q.s: Which Satavahana queen ruled as regent during her son's minority?
q.x: Naganika, wife of Satakarni I, acted as regent; Gautami Balasri issued the Nasik inscription.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Nagarjunakonda is correct?
o: It was discovered by A.H. Longhurst in 1902
Its monuments now lie under the Srisailam reservoir
Mahishasaka was the only Hinayana sect there
Yajnasri Satakarni built its monastery for Aryadeva
q.x: Discovered by A.R. Saraswati (1926) and excavated by Longhurst, it was drowned by the Nagarjunasagar reservoir; tradition links its monastery with Acharya Nagarjuna.

q.s: According to tradition, Yajnasri Satakarni built the Sriparvata monastery for:
q.x: Tradition holds Yajnasri built it for Acharya Nagarjuna.

q.s: Which of the following statements about religion in the Satavahana period is correct?
o: The kings followed the Vedic religion while their queens patronised Buddhism
The Satavahana kings and queens were all followers of Jainism
Buddhism received no royal patronage in the Satavahana period
The Satavahanas banned Vedic sacrifices in their kingdom
q.x: Vedic kings and Buddhist queens made the age pluralist.

q.s: Which of the following terms in Ikshvaku records is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Halikas were farmers; Kammaru were blacksmiths.

q.s: Rituals at the Srivari temple at Tirumala follow which Agama?
q.x: Vaikhanasa (a Vaishnava Agama) is followed at Tirumala.

q.s: The Kota family of Dharanikota in the Andhra region was subordinate to which dynasty?
q.x: The Kotas of Dharanikota were Kakatiya subordinates.

q.s: The Qutb Shahi dynasty was founded by a Bahmani governor of:
q.x: Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk, Bahmani governor of Telangana, founded the Golconda kingdom.

q.s: At the battle of Raichur (1520), Krishnadevaraya defeated:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya defeated Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur at Raichur in 1520.

q.s: Aliya Rama Raya of Vijayanagara was killed in which battle?
q.x: Rama Raya was killed at Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi), 1565; Golconda then took coastal Andhra.

q.s: The Thousand-Pillar Temple at Hanumakonda was built by:
q.x: Rudra Deva (Rudradeva I) built the Thousand-Pillar Temple.

q.s: The Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama is attributed to:
q.x: The Bhimeswara temple is attributed to the Eastern Chalukya Bhima I.

q.s: Srinatha, the great Telugu poet, was the court poet (Vidyadhikari) of which dynasty?
q.x: Srinatha served Pedakomati Vema Reddy of Kondavidu; his works include Haravilasam and Sivaratri Mahatyam.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Srinatha?
q.x: Shabda Ratnakaram is by Vamana Bhatta Bana.

q.s: What was the official court language of the Qutb Shahis of Golconda?
q.x: Persian was the court language, though the Qutb Shahis also patronised Telugu.

q.s: The Qutb Shahis shifted their capital from Golconda to Hyderabad in:
q.x: Hyderabad became the capital from 1592 under Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.

q.s: The Velanati ruler Prithvisvara was killed by which Kakatiya ruler?
q.x: Ganapatideva, with the Nellore Choda Tikkana, killed Prithvisvara.

q.s: Narasapuram, the chief shipbuilding centre of coastal Andhra in the 16th-17th centuries, is in which district?
q.x: Narasapuram is in West Godavari district.

q.s: Who is known as 'Andhra Tilak' and named the ceded districts 'Rayalaseema'?
q.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao coined the name Rayalaseema (1928).

q.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao became the first Telugu political prisoners in 1908 for articles in:
q.x: Their articles appeared in Gadicherla's Telugu Swarajya, hence the Swarajya case under s.124A.

q.s: The Kothapatnam summer school of 1937, which trained young activists in politics and economics, was banned by:
q.x: The Madras Government banned the Kothapatnam political school.

q.s: In the context of anti-zamindari and agency struggles, 'Pullari' was a:
q.x: Pullari was a grazing tax; Nazarana was the tenancy renewal fee and Gothi bonded labour in the Agency.

q.s: Which of the following terms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
o: Gothi – bonded labour in the Agency
q.x: Bedalli meant eviction for non-payment.

q.s: Garimella Satyanarayana was jailed in 1922 for his patriotic song:
q.x: Garimella was imprisoned for a year for 'Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu'.

q.s: 'Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu' was written by:
q.x: Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu is by Viswanatha Satyanarayana, the Jnanpith winner.

q.s: Which Telugu poet is known as 'Kavi Samrat'?
q.x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana is Kavi Samrat; Seshendra Sarma is Yuga Kavi.

q.s: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao, an Abhyudaya writer, was the editor of which magazine?
q.x: Kutumba Rao edited Chandamama for many years.

q.s: The English daily 'Swarajya' was started at Madras in 1921 by:
q.x: Tanguturi Prakasam started the Swarajya on 26 October 1921.

q.s: The Guntur newspaper 'Desabhimani' was earlier known as:
q.x: Desabhimani, run by Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao, was earlier Krishnavrittantini.

q.s: Who is known as 'Burrakatha Pitamaha'?
q.x: Shaik Nazar, born at Pannekallu (Guntur), received the Padma Shri in 1986.

q.s: Which of the following folk performances of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
o: Garagalu – decorated pots for the village goddess
q.x: Puli Veshalu is the tiger dance of Vizianagaram Dasara.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the end of the Hoysalas is correct?
o: Ballala III was killed at Kannanur by the Sultan of Madurai
Malik Kafur took Dwarasamudra from Vira Ballala II
The Hoysala territory passed to the Bahmanis
Vishnuvardhana was the last Hoysala ruler
q.x: Ballala III was killed by Ghiyas-ud-din of Madurai and the territory passed to Vijayanagara; Kafur took Dwarasamudra from Ballala III.

q.s: When Mahmud of Ghazni raided the Somnath temple in 1025, Gujarat was ruled by:
q.x: The Solanki Bhima I ruled Gujarat and rebuilt the temple after Mahmud left.

q.s: Who is regarded as India's first woman sociologist?
q.x: Irawati Karve, author of Kinship Organization in India, is regarded as India's first woman sociologist.

q.s: The book 'Homo Hierarchicus' (1966) on the Indian caste system was written by:
q.x: Homo Hierarchicus is by Louis Dumont.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Matrilineal family – descent through the father
Joint family – two or more generations
Patriarchal family – authority of the senior male
q.x: Matrilineal descent is traced through the mother.

q.s: Desertion by the husband, leaving the family to fend for itself, is often called:
q.x: Desertion is termed the poor man's divorce.

q.s: Under the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, 1939, a wife may seek divorce if maintenance has not been paid for:
q.x: Non-payment of maintenance for 2 years is a ground under the 1939 Act.

q.s: The concept of 'Great Tradition and Little Tradition' was given by:
q.x: Robert Redfield gave the concept; Milton Singer and McKim Marriott applied it to India.

q.s: In McKim Marriott's terms, the downward flow of elements from the great tradition to the little tradition is called:
q.x: The downward flow is parochialisation; the upward flow is universalisation.

q.s: Who described the Indian tribes as 'backward Hindus'?
q.x: G.S. Ghurye called them backward Hindus and argued for assimilation; Elwin favoured isolation.

q.s: The concept of 'ethnocentrism' is associated with:
q.x: W.G. Sumner introduced the term ethnocentrism in Folkways (1906).

q.s: Who described Indian villages as self-reliant 'little republics'?
q.x: Charles Metcalfe called Indian villages little republics.

q.s: The ethnic conflict in Manipur since May 2023 has been mainly between:
q.x: The Manipur conflict is between the Meiteis (seeking ST status) and the Kukis.

q.s: Which of the following ethnic conflicts is NOT correctly matched?
o: Assam Movement – Assamese vs Bengali migrants
q.x: In Tripura the conflict has been between indigenous tribes and Bengali settlers.

q.s: Which section of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 excludes members of notified Scheduled Tribes from its application?
q.x: Section 2(2) excludes notified STs unless the Centre directs otherwise; the Supreme Court upheld this in October 2025.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021 is correct?
o: It permits commercial surrogacy by close relatives
Only unmarried women can be surrogates
A woman may act as surrogate any number of times
q.x: The Act bans commercial surrogacy; the surrogate must be a married woman with a child of her own and can act only once.

q.s: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 (as amended) allows termination up to how many weeks for special categories of women?
q.x: The 2021 amendment allows 24 weeks for special categories.

q.s: The Communal G.O. of 1921, granting reservation to non-Brahmins, was won by:
q.x: The Justice Party government in Madras issued the Communal G.O. in 1921.

q.s: According to the Constitution's Eighth Schedule, how many official languages does India recognise?
q.x: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages; the census records about 1,635 mother tongues.

q.s: Under the POCSO Act, 2012, which court is designated as the Special Court in each district?
q.x: A Court of Session is designated as the POCSO Special Court.

q.s: The central share of the Fast Track Special Courts scheme (2019) for rape and POCSO cases is funded from the:
q.x: The central share of FTSCs comes from the Nirbhaya Fund.

q.s: Under Section 19 of the POCSO Act, failure to report an offence is punishable with imprisonment up to:
q.x: Failure to report is punishable with up to 6 months' imprisonment.

q.s: A Sukanya Samriddhi account can be opened with a minimum annual deposit of:
q.x: The minimum is ₹250 a year, for up to two girls in a family.

q.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is implemented under which component of Mission Shakti?
q.x: BBBP falls under Sambal; Samarthya covers empowerment schemes such as PM Matru Vandana.

q.s: PMAY-Gramin is implemented by which Union Ministry?
q.x: PMAY-G is run by the Ministry of Rural Development; PMAY-Urban is under Housing and Urban Affairs.

q.s: Unit assistance under PMAY-Gramin in hilly and North-Eastern areas is:
q.x: It is ₹1.30 lakh in hilly and NE areas and ₹1.20 lakh in the plains.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Deepam-2 scheme, eligible families receive:
q.x: Deepam-2 gives 3 free LPG refills a year; the original Deepam (1999) gave connections.

q.s: Which of the following old and new scheme names of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
o: YSR Pension Kanuka – NTR Bharosa Pension
q.x: Vidya Kanuka became Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan Vidyarthi Mitra; Amma Vodi became Talliki Vandanam.

q.s: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 came into force on:
q.x: It received assent on 11 September 1989 and came into force on 30 January 1990.

q.s: Which of the following Supreme Court cases is NOT correctly matched with its issue?
o: Jeeja Ghosh (2016) – deplaning of a woman with cerebral palsy
q.x: T.M.A. Pai held minority status is determined State-wise.

q.s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, 'differences' are referred to:
q.x: Questions go to the PIC, differences to a Neutral Expert and disputes to a Court of Arbitration.

q.s: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project connects Kolkata with Mizoram through which port of Myanmar?
q.x: The Kaladan project runs through Sittwe port.

q.s: The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway begins in India at:
q.x: The highway starts at Moreh in Manipur.

q.s: The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions, in force since 1998, lapsed in:
q.x: It lapsed on 31 March 2026 after MC14.

q.s: The 'Stability and Growth Pact' of the European Union aims to limit:
q.x: The Stability and Growth Pact limits budget deficits (3% of GDP) and public debt of EU members.

q.s: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is NOT borrowed from Britain?
q.x: Judicial review is from the USA; the Speaker, single citizenship and parliamentary privileges are British.

q.s: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by the:
q.x: The original Constitution had 8 Schedules; the 1st Amendment (1951) added the Ninth.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that no person shall be compelled to pay taxes for the promotion of a particular religion?
q.x: Article 27 bars such taxes; Article 26 gives freedom to manage religious affairs.

q.s: Which of the following Articles does NOT form part of the Right to Freedom of Religion?
q.x: Articles 25-28 cover freedom of religion; Article 29 is a cultural and educational right.

q.s: The right to property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the:
q.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) deleted it and made it a legal right under Article 300A.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court issue guidelines on arrest, including the arrest memo?
q.x: D.K. Basu (1997) laid down arrest guidelines; Lalita Kumari (2013) made FIR registration mandatory.

q.s: In Lalita Kumari (2013), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Handcuffing is permissible only in exceptional cases
Bail is the rule and jail the exception
Arrest is mandatory in dowry cases
Registration of FIR is mandatory for cognizable offences
q.x: Lalita Kumari made FIR registration mandatory for cognizable offences.

q.s: In January 2023, the Supreme Court upheld demonetisation by a majority of:
q.x: The 2016 demonetisation was upheld 4:1 under Section 26(2) of the RBI Act.

q.s: The Supreme Court's Article 370 judgment of December 2023 directed elections to the J&K Assembly by:
q.x: The Court set a deadline of 30 September 2024.

q.s: The Right to Information has been read by the courts into which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: RTI is a statutory right (RTI Act, 2005) and has been read into freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 is correct?
o: Human Rights Courts function at the district level under it
The NHRC was constituted on 10 December 1993
The Act came into force in 2006
It made the NHRC a constitutional body
q.x: The NHRC (a statutory body) was constituted on 12 October 1993; the Act is deemed in force from 28 September 1993.

q.s: Article 43B on co-operative societies was added to the Directive Principles by the:
q.x: Article 43B came by the 97th Amendment (2011), the latest DPSP addition.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court first hold that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights?
q.x: Golaknath (1967), an 11-judge bench, held that Parliament cannot abridge Fundamental Rights.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the amendability of Fundamental Rights is correct?
o: Shankari Prasad (1951) held that an amendment is 'law' under Article 13
Golaknath arose from a challenge to the 24th Amendment
Kesavananda Bharati was decided by an 11-judge bench
q.x: Shankari Prasad held an amendment is not 'law'; Golaknath (11 judges) concerned the 17th Amendment; Kesavananda had 13 judges.

q.s: Who acted as President of India in 1977 after the death of President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed?
q.x: Vice-President B.D. Jatti acted as President in 1977; Hidayatullah acted in 1969 after Zakir Husain's death.

q.s: A person elected President to fill a vacancy caused by the death of the President holds office for:
o: A full term of five years
The remainder of the predecessor's term
q.x: A President elected to fill a vacancy gets a full five-year term from the date of entering office.

q.s: Which of the following Articles relating to High Courts is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 218 – SC removal provisions applied to HC judges
Article 220 – restriction on practice after being a permanent judge
Article 222 – appointment of an acting Chief Justice
q.x: Article 222 deals with the transfer of judges; acting Chief Justices come under Article 223.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that the President and the Governor are not answerable to any court for the exercise of their powers?
q.x: Article 361 gives this immunity; in S.R. Bommai the Court still held their decisions reviewable for mala fides.

q.s: The Gauhati High Court has permanent benches at all of the following places EXCEPT:
q.x: Tripura has had its own High Court at Agartala since 2013; Kohima, Aizawl and Itanagar are Gauhati benches.

q.s: The principal seat of the Uttarakhand High Court is at:
q.x: The Uttarakhand High Court sits at Nainital.

q.s: Under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, the headquarters of the proposed National Tribunals Commission is at:
q.x: The Commission is to be headquartered at New Delhi, with five members chaired by a former SC judge or HC Chief Justice.

q.s: Part XIV-A of the Constitution, dealing with tribunals, was inserted by the:
q.x: Part XIV-A (Articles 323A and 323B) came by the 42nd Amendment.

q.s: Administrative tribunals for public service matters under Article 323A can be established by:
q.x: Article 323A tribunals can be set up only by Parliament; 323B tribunals by Parliament and State Legislatures.

q.s: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal'?
q.x: K.C. Wheare called it quasi-federal; Granville Austin used 'cooperative federalism'.

q.s: Which criterion carried the highest weight (45%) in the tax devolution formula of the 15th Finance Commission?
q.x: Income distance got 45%; tax and fiscal effort had the lowest weight, 2.5%.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a criterion in the 15th Finance Commission's devolution formula?
q.x: The criteria were income distance, population, area, forest and ecology, demographic performance, and tax and fiscal effort.

q.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act was enacted in:
q.x: The CAG's DPC Act was passed in 1971; a 1976 amendment separated accounts from audit.

q.s: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
q.x: The NCSC is constitutional (Article 338); the NCW, NCM and NHRC are statutory bodies.

q.s: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under which Union Ministry?
q.x: The office works under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, headquartered at New Delhi.

q.s: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by:
q.x: Transparency International publishes the CPI on a 0-100 scale, where a higher score means less corruption.

q.s: The Vohra Committee (1993) examined:
q.x: The N.N. Vohra Committee reported on the nexus between criminals, politicians and bureaucrats.

q.s: The Central Vigilance Commission became a statutory body in 2003 following the Supreme Court's judgment in:
q.x: Set up in 1964 by resolution, the CVC was given statutory status after Vineet Narain.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission is correct?
o: It was set up by an Act of Parliament in 1964
It has up to four Vigilance Commissioners
Its members hold office for four years or till 65, whichever is earlier
It was set up on the Vohra Committee's advice
q.x: Set up by resolution in 1964 (Santhanam Committee), the CVC has a CVC and up to two Vigilance Commissioners.

q.s: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh was promised in Parliament in 2014 by Prime Minister:
q.x: Manmohan Singh promised it in the Rajya Sabha, though it was not written into the AP Reorganisation Act.

q.s: For Special Category States, the central share of funding of Centrally Sponsored Schemes is:
q.x: Special Category States get 90% central funding of CSS.

q.s: The AIADMK was founded in 1972 by:
q.x: M.G. Ramachandran founded the AIADMK after breaking with the DMK in 1972.

q.s: Which of the following parties does NOT belong to the Janata Dal family?
q.x: RJD, JD(U), JD(S) and BJD come from the Janata Dal; the TDP was founded by N.T. Rama Rao in 1982.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment first froze the State-wise allocation of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 1971 Census?
q.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze it till 2000; the 84th extended the freeze till after 2026.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the freeze on delimitation is correct?
o: The 42nd Amendment froze seat allocation on the 2001 Census
The 87th Amendment increased the total number of Lok Sabha seats
The 84th Amendment extended the freeze till the first census after 2026
Delimitation is carried out by the Election Commission alone
q.x: The 42nd Amendment froze it on the 1971 Census; the 87th allowed readjustment on 2001 figures without changing seat totals.

q.s: The NOTA option was introduced following the Supreme Court's judgment in:
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013)
q.x: PUCL (September 2013) led to NOTA, first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014.

q.s: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed every year on:
q.x: 24 April marks the coming into force of the 73rd Amendment in 1993.

q.s: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by:
q.x: The WEF publishes the GGGI (since 2006); UNDP publishes the GDI and GII.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Gender Inequality Index is correct?
o: It is published by the World Economic Forum
It is measured on a 0-1 scale on which 1 is the worst
It is the ratio of female to male HDI
It is published by the Georgetown Institute
q.x: The UNDP's GII runs 0-1 with 1 the worst; the GDI is the female-to-male HDI ratio.

q.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1922-24 in the Andhra agency was led by:
q.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa rebellion; Vempatapu Satyam was a leader of the Srikakulam Girijan movement (1967-70).

q.s: The Planning Commission of India was set up on 15 March 1950 by:
o: A resolution of the Union Cabinet
q.x: It was set up by a Cabinet resolution and replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

q.s: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
q.x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman; the post carried Cabinet rank.

q.s: Appeals against the orders of SEBI lie to the:
q.x: Appeals against SEBI go to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

q.s: The Forward Markets Commission was merged with SEBI in:
q.x: The FMC was merged into SEBI in September 2015.

q.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) was set up under the:
q.x: IBBI was established under the IBC, 2016.

q.s: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) has its headquarters at:
q.x: IFSCA (2020) is the unified regulator of IFSCs, based at GIFT City, Gandhinagar.

q.s: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) was developed by:
q.x: UPI and BHIM were developed by the NPCI.

q.s: 'MeghRaj' is the Government of India's initiative for:
q.x: MeghRaj is the GI Cloud that hosts government applications.

q.s: Which State enacted India's first Right to Services law in 2010?
q.x: The Madhya Pradesh Lok Sewa Guarantee Act, 2010 was the first; Bihar followed in 2011.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Right to Services laws in India is correct?
o: Bihar enacted the first such law in 2010
They create a Fundamental Right under Article 21
They abolish all other grievance mechanisms
The concept grew out of the Citizens' Charter idea in Britain
q.x: Madhya Pradesh enacted the first law (2010); the laws add time-bound delivery and are statutory rights.

q.s: GRACE satellite studies show the most severe groundwater depletion in which part of India?
q.x: The worst depletion is in north-west India (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Delhi).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a category used by the CGWB for groundwater assessment units?
q.x: The categories are Safe, Semi-critical, Critical and Over-exploited.

q.s: The G-33 grouping in the WTO mainly focuses on:
q.x: The G-33 (2003) pursues food security, special products and the Special Safeguard Mechanism.

q.s: In the history of India's population growth, the period 1951-81 is described as a phase of:
q.x: 1901-21 was stagnant, 1921-51 steady, 1951-81 rapid, and 1981-2011 high but slowing.

q.s: Which year is called the 'Year of Great Divide' in India's demographic history?
q.x: 1921 marks the great divide, after which India's population grew continuously.

q.s: According to Census 2011, what was the share of Scheduled Castes in the population of present (residual) Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: SCs formed 17.08% of the population of residual AP; its sex ratio was 997.

q.s: The Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is expressed per:
q.x: MMR is maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births; IMR is per 1,000 live births.

q.s: The headquarters of the Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) is at:
q.x: APCRDA, set up under the APCRDA Act, 2014, is headquartered at Rayapudi.

q.s: Amaravati, the capital of Andhra Pradesh, is located in which mandal?
q.x: Amaravati lies in Thullur mandal on the Krishna, between Vijayawada and Guntur.

q.s: In the Ease of Living Index 2018, which city of Andhra Pradesh was ranked 4th?
q.x: Tirupati was ranked 4th among 111 cities in 2018.

q.s: Which of the following statements about MGNREGA is correct?
o: It confers a Fundamental Right to work under Article 21
It applies only to BPL families
It guarantees 200 days of work a year
It guarantees work within 5 km of the residence
q.x: MGNREGA gives a legal right to 100 days of work, within 5 km; it is not a Fundamental Right.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched on 1 May 2016 at:
q.x: PMUY was launched at Ballia, Uttar Pradesh, with the slogan 'Swachh Indhan Behtar Jeevan'.

q.s: Under the PM Ujjwala Yojana, the LPG connection is given in the name of:
o: An adult woman of the household
The male head of the household
q.x: The connection is issued in the name of an adult woman of a poor household.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's 'Talliki Vandanam' scheme, the annual assistance per school-going child is:
q.x: Talliki Vandanam gives ₹15,000 per child; Annadata Sukhibhava gives farmers ₹20,000 a year.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's 'Annadata Sukhibhava' scheme, farmers receive a year:
q.x: Annadata Sukhibhava gives ₹20,000 a year, including the PM-KISAN ₹6,000.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's nutrition services in plain areas, children aged 36-72 months at Anganwadi centres get:
o: A hot meal, an egg and 100 ml milk
q.x: They get a hot cooked meal, an egg and 100 ml milk; the tribal package is richer.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill, 2014 was passed by the Lok Sabha on:
q.x: The Lok Sabha passed it on 18 February 2014; the appointed day was 2 June 2014.

q.s: In the circular flow of income, the leakage 'taxes' is matched by the injection:
q.x: Saving matches investment, taxes government spending and imports exports.

q.s: In the circular flow of income, which of the following is NOT a leakage?
q.x: Exports are an injection; saving, taxes and imports are leakages.

q.s: In May 2026, MoSPI issued a uniform guideline for compiling Gross State Value Added with which base year?
q.x: The new guideline uses 2022-23 as the base year; APSES 2024-25 figures are still at 2011-12 prices.

q.s: In India, the income method of estimating national income is principally used for:
o: Services such as trade, transport and banking
q.x: The production method is used for agriculture, mining and manufacturing, the income method for services.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a method of measuring national income?
q.x: National income is measured by the product, income and expenditure methods.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT counted under 'Industry' in India's GVA classification?
q.x: Livestock is under agriculture and allied activities.

q.s: As per the India Employment Report 2024, which form of employment had a higher share in 2022 than regular wage/salaried employment?
q.x: Casual employment (22.7%) exceeded regular wage employment (21.5%) in 2022.

q.s: Which of the following statements about economic growth and development is correct?
o: Growth is a sufficient condition for development
Growth is quantitative while development is qualitative as well as quantitative
q.x: Growth is quantitative and value-neutral and can be negative; it is necessary but not sufficient for development, which is normative.

q.s: 'Inequality Reexamined' was written by:
q.x: Amartya Sen wrote Inequality Reexamined (1992).

q.s: Which of the following books is NOT correctly matched with its author?
o: The Economic History of India – R.C. Dutt
Principles of Political Economy and Taxation – Adam Smith
q.x: Principles of Political Economy and Taxation (rent, comparative advantage) is by David Ricardo.

q.s: A situation where more persons are engaged on a job than are needed, so that their marginal productivity is zero, is called:
q.x: Disguised unemployment is common in Indian agriculture and is not captured in headline rates.

q.s: Who wrote the 'People's Plan' (1944) for India's economic development?
q.x: M.N. Roy wrote the People's Plan; S.N. Agarwal the Gandhian Plan and J.P. Narayan the Sarvodaya Plan.

q.s: The Bombay Plan (1944) was prepared by:
q.x: Eight leading industrialists, including Tata and Birla, prepared the Bombay Plan.

q.s: The 'socialistic pattern of society' was adopted as the goal at which session of the Congress?
q.x: The Avadi session (1955) adopted it, shaping the Second Plan and IPR 1956.

q.s: The foundation stone of the Nagarjuna Sagar dam was laid by Jawaharlal Nehru on:
q.x: Nehru laid it on 10 December 1955.

q.s: The Prakasam Barrage is built across the Krishna at:
q.x: The Prakasam Barrage (1954-57) is at Vijayawada.

q.s: Which of the following is kept outside the divisible pool of central taxes shared with the States?
q.x: Cesses and surcharges are excluded, so effective devolution is only about 30-32%, below the headline 41%.

q.s: What is Andhra Pradesh's share in the divisible pool of central taxes as recommended by the 16th Finance Commission?
q.x: The 16th FC gave AP 4.217%; the 14th gave 4.305% and the 15th (2021-26) 4.047%.

q.s: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), attached to NITI Aayog, was set up in 2015 by merging:
q.x: DMEO (18 September 2015) merged the Programme Evaluation Office and the Independent Evaluation Office.

q.s: The National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD) was formerly known as:
q.x: NILERD, an autonomous institute under NITI Aayog, was formerly the Institute of Applied Manpower Research.

q.s: The CEO of NITI Aayog is appointed by the Prime Minister in the rank of:
o: Secretary to the Government of India
q.x: The CEO holds Secretary rank; the Vice-Chairperson holds Cabinet rank.

q.s: Which of the following statements about NITI Aayog is correct?
o: Its CEO holds Cabinet Minister rank
Its Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister and holds Cabinet rank
It was set up by an Act of Parliament
Its Governing Council is chaired by the President
q.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution in 2015; the PM chairs it and the CEO holds Secretary rank.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Payments Corporation of India is correct?
o: It is a not-for-profit company promoted by the RBI and the IBA
It is a statutory body created by the PSS Act, 2007
It launched the National Financial Switch in 2004
It is a department of the Reserve Bank of India
q.x: NPCI (2008) is authorised under the PSS Act; the NFS was launched by IDRBT in 2004 and taken over by NPCI in 2009.

q.s: Under India's flexible inflation targeting framework, the inflation target is set by:
o: The Government in consultation with the RBI
q.x: The Centre sets the target (4% CPI, +/-2%) in consultation with the RBI; the MPC sets the policy rate.

q.s: The term 'shadow banking' was coined in 2007 by:
q.x: Paul McCulley of PIMCO coined the term in 2007.

q.s: Chit funds in India are regulated under the Chit Funds Act, 1982 by:
q.x: Chit funds are regulated by the State Governments.

q.s: Under the Finance Act, 2019, the regulation of housing finance companies was transferred from the National Housing Bank to:
q.x: HFC regulation moved to the RBI; NHB kept supervision and refinance.

q.s: Andhra Bank was founded in 1923 by:
q.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam and Andhra Insurance (1925).

q.s: Canara Bank was founded at Mangaluru in 1906 by:
q.x: Ammembal Subba Rao Pai founded Canara Bank; Lajpat Rai was linked to Punjab National Bank.

q.s: Inflation described as 'too much money chasing too few goods' is:
q.x: Demand-pull inflation arises when aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply; cost-push comes from rising factor prices.

q.s: Which of the following types of inflation is NOT correctly matched with its cause?
o: Demand-pull – aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply
Cost-push – rise in wages and raw-material prices
Structural – supply bottlenecks and poor farm productivity
q.x: Export-led inflation comes from strong export demand draining domestic supply.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a revenue expenditure of the Union Government?
q.x: Building highways creates assets and is capital expenditure; the others are recurring revenue items.

q.s: According to Andhra Pradesh's Budget Estimates 2026-27, the State's fiscal deficit is what percentage of GSDP?
q.x: AP's BE 2026-27 shows a fiscal deficit of 3.84% and a revenue deficit of 1.11% of GSDP.

q.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the Centre's fiscal deficit in FY26 was:
q.x: Buoyant revenues helped bring the fiscal deficit to 4.4% of GDP in FY26.

q.s: A cut motion that seeks to reduce a demand to ₹1, expressing disapproval of the policy behind it, is called:
q.x: Policy cut reduces the demand to ₹1; token cut by ₹100; economy cut by a specified amount.

q.s: In the budget process, putting all outstanding demands for grants to vote on the last day without discussion is called:
q.x: The guillotine is applied by the Speaker on the last allotted day.

q.s: The 'Purvodaya' plan announced in the Union Budget 2024-25 covers all of the following States EXCEPT:
q.x: Purvodaya covers Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Public Account of India constituted?
q.x: Article 266(2) creates the Public Account; withdrawals from it need no parliamentary appropriation.

q.s: India's services trade surplus reached a record of about how much in FY25?
q.x: The services surplus touched a record $188.8 billion in FY25; services were about 49% of total exports.

q.s: Cropping intensity is calculated as:
o: Net sown area / Gross cropped area x 100
Gross cropped area / Net sown area x 100
Net irrigated area / Net sown area x 100
Gross cropped area / Total area x 100
q.x: Cropping intensity = GCA / NSA x 100.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of the nine-fold land-use classification?
q.x: Net irrigated area is not one of the nine land-use categories.

q.s: The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) is one of the eight missions under:
o: The National Action Plan on Climate Change
The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture
q.x: NMSA is one of the NAPCC's eight missions; since 2022-23 it is under PM-RKVY.

q.s: 'Operation Barga' (1978), which recorded the names of sharecroppers, was launched in:
q.x: Operation Barga was a West Bengal land reform for registering bargadars.

q.s: Which of the following statements about land reforms in India is correct?
o: Consolidation of holdings succeeded mainly in Punjab, Haryana and western UP
Consolidation of holdings succeeded most in Kerala and Tamil Nadu
Operation Barga was a land reform of Bihar
Operation Barga abolished all intermediaries in 1950
q.x: Consolidation succeeded in the north-west but failed to take off in Tamil Nadu and Kerala; Operation Barga (1978) was West Bengal's.

q.s: Operation Greens, launched for tomato, onion and potato, is implemented by which Ministry?
q.x: Operation Greens (Budget 2018-19) is run by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries; it was widened to TOTAL in 2021-22.

q.s: Negotiable warehouse receipts and warehouses in India are accredited by:
q.x: The WDRA, set up under the WDR Act, 2007, accredits warehouses and NWRs.

q.s: The Central Warehousing Corporation was set up in:
q.x: The CWC was set up on 2 March 1957.

q.s: Under the Decentralised Procurement scheme introduced in 1997:
o: States themselves procure, store and distribute foodgrains
q.x: Under DCP the States procure, store and distribute the grain under the PDS.

q.s: In the new IIP series, what is the weight of manufacturing?
q.x: Manufacturing has a weight of 76.1% and mining 11.1% in the new series, based on 2022-23 GVA shares.

q.s: After a sector is delicensed, an industrial unit has only to file:
q.x: A delicensed unit only files an IEM with the DPIIT.

q.s: National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) were introduced under:
q.x: NIMZs come under the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011; Prakasam NIMZ got final approval in 2016.

q.s: What was India's rank in the World Bank's Doing Business 2015 report?
q.x: India was 142nd in Doing Business 2015 and rose to 63rd in Doing Business 2020.

q.s: Which country topped the World Bank's Doing Business 2019 and 2020 rankings?
q.x: New Zealand topped both years.

q.s: Rehabilitation of a sick industrial unit requires effective coordination among:
q.x: Sickness hits lenders, workers and the exchequer alike, so all must coordinate.

q.s: Industrial sickness in India has been concentrated in all of the following industries EXCEPT:
q.x: Sickness has hit textiles, jute, sugar and engineering, not software.

q.s: In 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh's per capita income was about how many times India's per capita income?
q.x: AP's PCI exceeded India's by about ₹75,000, about 1.34 times.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh has the third-longest coastline in India. Its length is about:
q.x: AP kept the entire coastline of about 1,053 km, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Which component forms the largest share of Andhra Pradesh's public debt?
q.x: Market loans form about 75% of AP's public debt; Central loans are only about 8%.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the share of the debt of the undivided State allotted to Andhra Pradesh was about:
q.x: AP took about 58% of the debt but got about 46% of revenue.

q.s: The Polavaram Ordinance, 2014 transferred submergence mandals of which district from Telangana to Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Seven mandals of Khammam district went to AP to ease Polavaram resettlement.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, State employees who did not opt for a State were allotted on the basis of:
q.x: Non-opters were allotted on the basis of native status.

q.s: The Centre's refusal of Special Category Status to Andhra Pradesh was partly based on fear of similar demands from:
q.x: The domino fear was of identical demands from Bihar and Odisha; the Centre offered a special assistance package.

q.s: Under the NARP, how many agro-climatic zones does present Andhra Pradesh have?
q.x: Residual AP has six agro-climatic zones; undivided AP had seven.

q.s: The Model Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (APLM) Act, 2017 provides for:
o: Minimum support prices for all crops
Declaring the whole State a single market
q.x: The Model APLM Act makes the whole State a single unified market.

q.s: Guntur Mirchi Yard is Asia's largest market for:
q.x: Guntur Mirchi Yard is Asia's largest chilli market; Guntur also has an Agri Export Zone for red chillies.

q.s: Which town of Andhra Pradesh has the second largest market yard in the State?
q.x: Adoni (Kurnool) has the second largest market yard, after Guntur.

q.s: The Central Sector Scheme for the formation of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organisations has an outlay of:
q.x: The scheme, implemented through SFAC, NABARD, NCDC and NAFED, has an outlay of ₹6,860 crore.

q.s: The apex organisation of the Cooperative Marketing Societies in Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: AP MARKFED is the apex body; the DCMSs procure produce, also on its behalf.

q.s: The 'Golden Revolution' is associated with:
q.x: Golden Revolution = horticulture (and honey); Yellow = oilseeds; Round = potato.

q.s: Which of the following revolutions is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Pink Revolution is meat and poultry; Blue is fisheries.

q.s: The National Dairy Development Board, which implemented Operation Flood, was set up in 1965 at:
q.x: NDDB was set up at Anand; the National Dairy Research Institute is at Karnal.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Operation Flood is correct?
o: It ran from 1970 to 1996 in three phases
It was modelled on Kerala's milk cooperatives
It aimed at increasing fish production
q.x: Operation Flood was run by the NDDB on the Anand pattern.

q.s: The Single Desk Portal of Andhra Pradesh, launched in April 2015, is a platform of which kind?
q.x: It is a G2B platform for investor clearances under the Single Desk Policy 2015-20.

q.s: Krishnapatnam in Andhra Pradesh is a node of which industrial corridor?
q.x: Krishnapatnam is the AP node of the CBIC; Orvakal is an HBIC node and Kopparthy a VCIC node.

q.s: Orvakal, an industrial node in Kurnool district, falls on which corridor?
q.x: Orvakal is a node of the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

q.s: The Collateralised Borrowing and Lending Obligation (CBLO) has been replaced by:
q.x: CBLO, operated by the CCIL from 2003, was replaced by TREPS.

q.s: Commercial Paper and Certificates of Deposit were introduced in India on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Vaghul Committee led to CDs (1989) and CP (1990).

q.s: Which is the only continent crossed by the Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn?
q.x: Africa alone is crossed by the Equator and both Tropics.

q.s: The Arctic Circle passes through all of the following countries EXCEPT:
q.x: The Arctic Circle (66½°N) crosses Norway, Sweden and Finland, but not the UK.

q.s: The westernmost longitude of India, 68°7'E, lies at:
q.x: Guhar Moti in Kutch marks the western end; the easternmost point is near 97°25'E in Arunachal Pradesh.

q.s: Active volcanoes are absent in the Himalayas because the Himalayas were formed by:
q.x: Continental collision produces no magma, unlike subduction margins such as the Andes.

q.s: According to the FAO's Status of the World's Soil Resources 2026 report, the leading threat to soils is:
q.x: Soil erosion ranks first, followed by loss of soil organic carbon and nutrient mismanagement.

q.s: Soils formed in place from the underlying parent rock are called:
q.x: In-situ (residual) soils are called sedentary soils.

q.s: What is the ultimate base level of a river?
q.x: Sea level is the ultimate base level; a lake or dam is a local base level.

q.s: When a stream erodes headward, breaches a divide and diverts the upper waters of a neighbouring stream, it is called:
q.x: This is stream (river) capture or piracy.

q.s: The Belum Caves in Andhra Pradesh are formed in:
q.x: Belum is a karst cave in black limestone in Nandyal (formerly Kurnool) district.

q.s: The Belum Caves were first recorded in 1884 by:
q.x: Robert Bruce Foote recorded them in 1884; in June 2025 they were declared a GSI Geo-Heritage Site.

q.s: India's continental shelf is broadest off the coast of:
q.x: The shelf is broadest off Gujarat (Gulf of Khambhat) on the west coast.

q.s: Which is the only major port of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Visakhapatnam is AP's only major port; the others are non-major ports.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Benelux group?
q.x: Benelux is Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg; Denmark is called the country of winds.

q.s: Which is the smallest of the four main islands of Japan?
q.x: Shikoku is the smallest; Honshu is the largest and holds the Kanto plain.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four main islands of Japan?
q.x: The four main islands are Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu.

q.s: Western disturbances that bring winter rain to north-west India are brought by the:
q.x: The Sub-Tropical Westerly Jet lies south of the Himalayas in winter and brings western disturbances; its shift north in June marks the monsoon onset.

q.s: Where has India's lowest temperature been recorded?
q.x: Dras in Ladakh holds India's lowest recorded temperature; Ganganagar records some of the highest.

q.s: Including cold deserts, which is the largest desert in the world?
q.x: Antarctica, a cold desert, is the largest; the Sahara is the largest hot desert.

q.s: Which region has the largest tropical rainforest in the world?
q.x: The Amazon is the largest; the Congo Basin is second.

q.s: Teak and sal, which shed their leaves in the dry season, are typical trees of the:
q.x: Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests have teak and sal.

q.s: In Koeppen's climatic classification, the second letter 'f' denotes:
q.x: f = no dry season; m = monsoon; w = dry winter; s = dry summer.

q.s: According to the IMD, which year was India's warmest since 1901?
q.x: 2024 was India's warmest year (+0.65°C anomaly); the 2025 anomaly was lower (+0.28°C).

q.s: Which of the following statements about tides is correct?
o: Neap tides occur at the first and third quarters of the Moon
Spring tides have the minimum tidal range
Perigean tides occur when the Moon is farthest from the Earth
Neap tides occur at new moon and full moon
q.x: Spring tides (maximum range) come at new and full moon; perigean tides are high because the Moon is closest.

q.s: The Grand Banks fishing ground lies near:
q.x: The Grand Banks lie off Newfoundland, where the cold Labrador Current meets the warm Gulf Stream.

q.s: Ocean currents influence the climate of coastal regions mainly because they:
q.x: Currents carry heat from low to high latitudes, warming or cooling the coasts they pass.

q.s: What is the capital of the Union Territory of Lakshadweep?
q.x: Kavaratti is the capital; Agatti has the airport.

q.s: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands share maritime borders with all of the following countries EXCEPT:
q.x: The islands' maritime neighbours are Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia.

q.s: The Indian Standard Meridian (82°30' E) passes near Mirzapur in which State?
q.x: Mirzapur is in Uttar Pradesh; the meridian also crosses MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The Indian Standard Meridian passes through all of the following States EXCEPT:
q.x: The meridian crosses UP, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, not Telangana.

q.s: According to the revised measurement, the length of India's coastline is about:
q.x: The revised coastline is 11,098.81 km; the rise from 7,516.6 km came from finer GIS tracing, not real growth.

q.s: According to Burrard's regional divisions, the Kumaon Himalaya lies between the rivers:
q.x: Punjab (Indus-Sutlej), Kumaon (Sutlej-Kali), Nepal (Kali-Teesta), Assam (Teesta-Dihang).

q.s: Which of the following Himalayan divisions is NOT correctly matched with its bounding rivers?
q.x: The Assam Himalaya lies between the Teesta and the Dihang.

q.s: Which is the highest peak lying wholly within India?
q.x: Nanda Devi in the Kumaon Himalaya is the highest wholly within India; Kanchenjunga lies on the Nepal border.

q.s: The Lesser Himalaya is also known as the:
q.x: The Lesser Himalaya is the Himachal; Himadri is the Greater Himalaya.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Lesser Himalaya is correct?
o: It is also called the Himadri
It lies to the south of the Shiwalik
The Mahabharat Lekh of Nepal belongs to the Greater Himalaya
The Pir Panjal range runs from the Jhelum to the upper Beas
q.x: The Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) lies between the Himadri and the Shiwalik; the Mahabharat Lekh continues it.

q.s: Which of the following valleys is NOT correctly matched with its State?
q.x: The Lahaul Valley is in Himachal Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Shiwalik range is correct?
o: It is the oldest of the three Himalayan ranges
It lies to the north of the Himachal
It is the youngest and outermost range, made of unconsolidated sediments
q.x: The Shiwalik is the youngest, southernmost range; the granite core belongs to the Himadri.

q.s: On the Malabar coast, the backwaters are locally called:
q.x: Kayals are backwaters; teris are coastal dunes.

q.s: Palnadu district of Andhra Pradesh was carved out in 2022 from which district?
q.x: Palnadu was carved from Guntur and is part of Coastal Andhra.

q.s: Which of the following districts of Andhra Pradesh is most prone to drought rather than cyclones?
q.x: Inland Anantapur in Rayalaseema is drought-prone; the coastal districts face cyclones.

q.s: Which is the largest riverine island in the world?
q.x: Majuli on the Brahmaputra in Assam is the largest riverine island.

q.s: Which of the following is the easternmost tributary of the Ganga?
q.x: The Mahananda is the easternmost tributary; the Yamuna is the westernmost.

q.s: In Bangladesh, the Brahmaputra is known as the:
q.x: The Brahmaputra is the Jamuna in Bangladesh; the Ganga is the Padma.

q.s: The Hirakud dam, one of the longest earthen dams, is built across which river?
q.x: Hirakud is on the Mahanadi near Sambalpur, Odisha.

q.s: The Mahanadi river rises at:
q.x: The Mahanadi rises at Sihawa in Chhattisgarh.

q.s: Which State has the largest area under black soil in India?
q.x: Maharashtra has the largest area under black (regur) soil.

q.s: Black soil is found in all of the following regions EXCEPT:
q.x: Black soil covers the Deccan lava region; it is not found in the Himalayas.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the term 'Chalka' refers to:
q.x: Chalka denotes red sandy soils; Dubba denotes red loamy sands.

q.s: The characteristic tree of the Sundarbans mangrove forest is:
q.x: The Sundarbans take their name from the Sundari tree.

q.s: Mangrove forests are found in all of the following States EXCEPT:
q.x: Mangroves occur in every coastal State but not in landlocked Assam.

q.s: Under the Disaster Management framework, the National Crisis Management Committee is headed by the:
q.x: The NCMC is headed by the Cabinet Secretary; the National Executive Committee by the Union Home Secretary.

q.s: Which of the following disaster management bodies is NOT correctly matched with its head?
o: National Crisis Management Committee – Cabinet Secretary
State Crisis Management Committee – Chief Secretary
National Executive Committee – Union Home Secretary
q.x: The High Level Committee is headed by the Union Home Minister.

q.s: How many battalions does the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) now have?
q.x: The NDRF began with 8 and now has 16 battalions, drawn from the central armed police forces.

q.s: NDRF personnel are drawn on deputation from all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: NDRF draws from the central armed police forces (BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, SSB), not the Army.

q.s: The 'Blue Revolution' is associated with:
q.x: Blue = fish; Yellow = oilseeds; Golden = horticulture and honey; Grey = fertilisers.

q.s: The 'Grey Revolution' relates to:
q.x: The Grey Revolution refers to fertilisers.

q.s: The Bhilai Steel Plant was set up with the collaboration of:
q.x: Bhilai was built with Soviet help; Rourkela with West Germany and Durgapur with the UK.

q.s: Which of the following steel plants is NOT correctly matched with its collaborating country?
q.x: Bokaro was built with Soviet help.

q.s: The SEZ Act, 2005 came into force on:
q.x: The SEZ Act came into force on 10 February 2006.

q.s: Which State has the largest number of operational SEZs in India?
q.x: Tamil Nadu has the most operational SEZs.

q.s: The Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) was incorporated in:
q.x: SAIL was incorporated on 24 January 1973 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an integrated steel plant of SAIL?
q.x: Salem is a special steel plant of SAIL.

q.s: India's first semiconductor fabrication unit (Tata-PSMC) is being set up at:
q.x: The fab is at Dholera, Gujarat; Micron's ATMP unit is at Sanand and Tata's ATMP plant at Jagiroad, Assam.

q.s: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in:
q.x: The ISM was launched in December 2021.

q.s: High-pressure boilers of BHEL are made at its unit in:
q.x: BHEL makes high-pressure boilers at Tiruchirappalli.

q.s: BHEL's Ramachandrapuram unit is located near:
q.x: Ramachandrapuram is in Hyderabad.

q.s: The Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) rankings of States are released by:
q.x: BRAP is released by DPIIT; BRAP 2020 placed States in categories such as 'top achievers'.

q.s: India's first official airmail flight in 1911 flew from Allahabad to:
q.x: The airmail flight of 18 February 1911 went from Allahabad to Naini.

q.s: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced which Act?
q.x: It replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934 from January 2025.

q.s: The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram is being developed by:
q.x: GMR is the developer under PPP-DBFOT; it is AP's first greenfield airport since 2014.

q.s: Bhogapuram International Airport is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Bhogapuram is in Vizianagaram district.

q.s: Which of the following World Heritage Sites is NOT correctly matched with its State?
q.x: Khajuraho is in Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: The Moidams, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2024, are the burial mounds of which dynasty?
q.x: The Moidams of the Ahom dynasty are in Assam.

q.s: Which site became India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2026?
q.x: Sarnath became the 45th site at the 48th session in Busan.

q.s: The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched on 22 January 2015 at:
q.x: BBBP was launched at Panipat, Haryana.

q.s: Which State started the 'Cradle Baby Scheme' against female infanticide in 1992?
q.x: Tamil Nadu started the Cradle Baby Scheme in 1992.

q.s: Which is the largest stream of internal migration in India?
q.x: Rural-to-rural, mainly of women after marriage, is the largest stream.

q.s: Who led the 'People of India' project of the Anthropological Survey of India launched in 1985?
q.x: K.S. Singh led the project, which covered about 4,635 communities.

q.s: The Dongaria Kondh tribe lives in the hills of:
q.x: The Dongaria Kondh live in the Niyamgiri hills of Odisha.

q.s: Which of the following tribes is NOT correctly matched with its habitat?
q.x: The Dongaria Kondh live in the Niyamgiri hills of Odisha.

q.s: PM-JANMAN is a mission meant for the development of:
q.x: PM-JANMAN covers 75 PVTGs with 11 interventions.

q.s: Which of the following tribal schemes is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan aims to train 20 lakh grassroots leaders.

q.s: The Khasi language belongs to which language family?
q.x: Khasi, with Santali, Ho and Mundari, is Austro-Asiatic.

q.s: Which of the following languages does NOT belong to the Austro-Asiatic family?
q.x: Lepcha is Tibeto-Chinese.

q.s: Which of the following statements about PVTGs is correct?
o: The Sentinelese are among the largest PVTGs
The Chenchu are a PVTG of Tamil Nadu
The Sahariya are the largest PVTG
The Baiga are a PVTG of Kerala
q.x: The Sahariya are the largest; the Baiga are a PVTG of Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: The Chenchu, a PVTG, are mainly found in:
q.x: The Chenchus live in the Nallamala forests of AP and Telangana.

q.s: Which of the following communities was NOT among the five notified as national minorities in 1993?
q.x: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified in 1993; Jains were added in 2014.

q.s: The '30x30' target to protect 30% of land and ocean by 2030 was adopted under the:
q.x: The 30x30 target came with the Kunming-Montreal GBF at CBD COP15 in December 2022.

q.s: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, a Community Reserve can be declared on:
o: Private or community land offered voluntarily
Government land adjoining a National Park
q.x: Community Reserves are on private or community land; Conservation Reserves are on government land linking protected areas.

q.s: Which of the following provides the highest degree of protection under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972?
q.x: A National Park gives higher protection than a sanctuary; no rights or grazing are allowed in it.

q.s: The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve of Andhra Pradesh was notified in:
q.x: Seshachalam BR was notified in 2010 in the Seshachalam hills of the southern Eastern Ghats.

q.s: Which is the largest National Park in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Papikonda (about 1,012.90 sq km) is the largest; Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) NP in Kadapa is the smallest.

q.s: Which was the first National Park of Andhra Pradesh (1989)?
q.x: Sri Venkateswara NP (1989) was the first; Mrugavani is in Telangana.

q.s: In the fifth (declining) stage of the demographic transition, population falls because:
o: Birth rate and death rate are both high
Birth rate falls below the death rate
Death rate falls sharply while birth rate stays high
q.x: Births fall below deaths, as in Japan and Germany.

q.s: What is the replacement-level Total Fertility Rate?
q.x: Replacement-level TFR is 2.1; the world average (about 2.2) is still slightly above it.

q.s: Which country recorded the world's lowest Total Fertility Rate (0.72) in 2023?
q.x: South Korea had the lowest TFR; Niger has the highest (about 6.6).

q.s: Zero Budget Natural Farming was pioneered by:
q.x: Subhash Palekar pioneered ZBNF; AP has adopted it widely.

q.s: Norman Borlaug, father of the Green Revolution, received the Nobel Peace Prize in:
q.x: Borlaug, who developed semi-dwarf wheat in Mexico, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

q.s: For general-category States, the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) is shared between the Centre and the State in the ratio:
q.x: SDRF is shared 75:25 for general States (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States).

q.s: Who is the ex officio President of the Governing Board of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)?
o: The Union Minister of Science and Technology
q.x: The Prime Minister heads the ANRF Governing Board; ANRF subsumed SERB.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Anusandhan National Research Foundation is correct?
o: Its Governing Board is headed by the Union S&T Minister
It was created by the ANRF Act, 2023
It was set up under the Companies Act, 2013
q.x: ANRF subsumed SERB, and the Prime Minister heads its Governing Board.

q.s: Gains from transfer of virtual digital assets (crypto-assets) in India are taxed at:
q.x: VDA gains are taxed at a flat 30%, losses cannot be set off, and 1% TDS applies on transfers.

q.s: NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), the commercial arm of ISRO, is headquartered at:
q.x: NSIL (2019) is a Department of Space CPSE based at Bengaluru.

q.s: The Indian private space firm Digantara works mainly in the field of:
q.x: Digantara works on space situational awareness; Pixxel on hyperspectral imaging; Dhruva Space (Hyderabad) on nanosatellite platforms.

q.s: India's first green hydrogen blending project in the city gas (PNG) network is at:
q.x: NTPC and Gujarat Gas started the project at Kawas, Surat, with 5% blending.

q.s: Which body is the nodal authority for the Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India?
q.x: The BEE is the nodal authority; the Standard caps emissions at 2 kg CO2-eq per kg of hydrogen.

q.s: The use of micro-organisms to remove pollutants such as oil spills and heavy metals from the environment is called:
q.x: Bioremediation uses microbes (sometimes genetically engineered) to clean up pollutants.

q.s: The VEGA series of indigenous RISC-V processors was developed by:
q.x: VEGA is from C-DAC; SHAKTI is from IIT Madras. The DIR-V programme was launched by MeitY.

q.s: NavIC, India's regional navigation satellite system, was developed by:
q.x: NavIC is ISRO's system; GAGAN was developed by ISRO with the Airports Authority of India.

q.s: Which of the following statements about NavIC is correct?
o: It is a global navigation system
It keeps its own IRNSS Network Time
q.x: NavIC is ISRO's regional system with its own time standard.

q.s: The satellites of the Global Positioning System (GPS) orbit the Earth at an altitude of about:
q.x: GPS satellites orbit at about 20,200 km, circling the Earth twice a day.

q.s: Who was China's first astronaut?
q.x: Yang Liwei flew on Shenzhou-5 in October 2003, making China the third nation to launch humans on its own.

q.s: Who was the first American to orbit the Earth?
q.x: John Glenn orbited the Earth in 1962; Alan Shepard was the first American in space.

q.s: The Information Fusion Centre - Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) set up by the Indian Navy in 2018 is located at:
q.x: IFC-IOR is at Gurugram.

q.s: A new submarine base of the Eastern Naval Command is coming up at:
q.x: The new base is at Rambilli near Visakhapatnam.

q.s: 'Rajendra' is the fire-control radar of which missile system?
q.x: Rajendra is Akash's fire-control radar; Swordfish is the long-range tracking radar of the BMD shield.

q.s: INS Astradharini, India's first indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel, was commissioned in 2015 at:
q.x: INS Astradharini was commissioned at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: In the name of the DRDO system 'SMART', the letter 'T' stands for:
q.x: SMART is the Supersonic Missile Assisted Release of Torpedo.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a deployment model of the MeghRaj (GI Cloud) initiative?
q.x: MeghRaj's four models are public, private, hybrid and community.

q.s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, a 'child' whose data needs verifiable parental consent is a person below:
q.x: Parental consent is needed below 18; targeted advertising at and behavioural monitoring of children are barred.

q.s: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, which of the following is permitted with respect to children's personal data?
q.x: Processing needs verifiable parental consent; tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising at children are barred.

q.s: Under the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010, the operator's liability was capped at:
q.x: Operator liability was no-fault and capped at ₹1,500 crore; Section 17(b) gave recourse against suppliers.

q.s: The SHANTI Act, 2025 permits foreign direct investment in nuclear power companies up to:
q.x: The SHANTI Act allows FDI up to 49%.

q.s: Under the 'fleet mode' programme approved in 2017, how many 700 MW PHWRs are to be built?
q.x: Ten 700 MW PHWRs are being built in fleet mode.

q.s: The Gorakhpur nuclear power project is located in which State?
q.x: Gorakhpur Haryana Anu Vidyut Pariyojana is in Fatehabad district of Haryana.

q.s: The Simhadri Super Thermal Power Plant in Andhra Pradesh belongs to:
q.x: Simhadri (2,000 MW) at Visakhapatnam is NTPC's; Krishnapatnam's Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS belongs to APPDCL.

q.s: National Energy Conservation Day is observed in India on:
q.x: It is observed on 14 December; the awards are given by the Ministry of Power through BEE.

q.s: The Machkund hydroelectric project is a joint project of Andhra Pradesh and:
q.x: Machkund is a joint AP-Odisha project.

q.s: The Pinnapuram integrated renewable energy storage project is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Pinnapuram is in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district; the Gandikota pumped storage project is in YSR Kadapa.

q.s: Kolleru lake of Andhra Pradesh, lying between the Godavari and Krishna deltas, is a:
q.x: Kolleru is a freshwater lake; Pulicat is a brackish lagoon on the AP-Tamil Nadu border.

q.s: Which of the following sites of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Nallamala and Seshachalam are Eastern Ghats forests.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Western Ghats panels is correct?
o: The Gadgil panel recommended treating the whole Western Ghats as ecologically sensitive
The Kasturirangan group limited the ESA to the cultural landscape
The Gadgil panel was set up after opposition to the Kasturirangan report
The Kasturirangan group declared 75% of the Ghats an ESA
q.x: Madhav Gadgil's WGEEP proposed the whole range; the later Kasturirangan group limited the ESA to the natural landscape, about 37%.

q.s: In north-west India, dust storms are most common during:
q.x: Dust storms peak in the hot, dry pre-monsoon months of April-June.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a protected-area category under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972?
q.x: Biosphere Reserves come under UNESCO's MAB programme, not the WPA.

q.s: In the term CCUS, the letter 'U' stands for:
q.x: CCUS is Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage: captured CO2 is used or stored.

q.s: The '30x30' target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework is:
q.x: 30x30 is Target 3; Target 22 concerns indigenous peoples and local communities.

q.s: National Dolphin Day in India is observed on:
q.x: 5 October marks the day in 2009 the Ganges River Dolphin was declared the National Aquatic Animal.

q.s: The Ganges River Dolphin was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in:
q.x: It was declared the National Aquatic Animal in 2009; Project Dolphin came in 2020.

q.s: The LG Polymers gas leak at Visakhapatnam in May 2020 involved:
q.x: LG Polymers leaked styrene; methyl isocyanate was the Bhopal gas.

q.s: Which of the following e-waste constituents mainly harms the kidneys and bones?
q.x: Cadmium harms kidney and bone (Itai-itai disease); mercury harms brain and kidney.

q.s: Under the CPCB's classification of industries, the practically non-polluting category is:
q.x: White is practically non-polluting; Red industries have a Pollution Index of 60 or more; Blue was added in 2025.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a colour category of industries under the CPCB classification?
q.x: The categories are Red, Orange, Green, White and, from 2025, Blue.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the early Ganga programmes is correct?
o: The Central Ganga Authority became the National Ganga Council in 1995
Namami Gange came before Ganga Action Plan-I
Ganga Action Plan-I was launched at Haridwar
Ganga Action Plan-I covered 25 main-stem towns
q.x: GAP-I was launched at Varanasi by Rajiv Gandhi; in 1995 the CGA became the National River Conservation Authority.

q.s: The use of plants to take up heavy metals from contaminated soil is called:
q.x: Phytoremediation uses plants (hyperaccumulators); bioaugmentation adds microbes.

q.s: Which of the following remediation methods is NOT correctly matched?
o: Biostimulation – adding nutrients for native microbes
Biosparging – injecting air below the water table
q.x: Phytoremediation uses plants to take up pollutants such as heavy metals.

q.s: Radon gas in soil is produced mainly by the decay of:
q.x: Radon comes from the decay of uranium and radium; after smoking it is a major cause of lung cancer.

q.s: DDT is listed as a persistent organic pollutant under which convention?
q.x: DDT is a POP under the Stockholm Convention; the Minamata Convention covers mercury.

q.s: The Central Zoo Authority (1992) was set up under which Act?
q.x: The CZA was set up under the WPA, 1972.

q.s: Central Government approval for diverting forest land to non-forest purposes is required under the:
q.x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires central approval.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the EIA public hearing is correct?
o: Category A projects are exempt from it
It is conducted by the National Green Tribunal
It is conducted by the SPCB with the District Collector presiding
No prior notice is required for it
q.x: 30 days' notice is given and the hearing is completed within 45 days; B2 and strategic projects are exempt.

q.s: 'The One-Straw Revolution' (1975), a classic on natural farming, was written by:
q.x: Masanobu Fukuoka wrote it; permaculture is associated with Mollison and Holmgren.

q.s: Which is the largest natural source of methane?
q.x: Wetlands are the largest natural source; flooded paddy fields are a major agricultural source.

q.s: Application of nitrogen fertilisers to crops mainly releases which greenhouse gas?
q.x: Nitrogen fertilisers release nitrous oxide through soil microbes.

q.s: A climate 'tipping point' refers to:
o: The year in which global emissions reach their peak
A threshold beyond which small changes trigger large, irreversible shifts
The point at which a country reaches net-zero emissions
The temperature at which mountain glaciers begin to melt
q.x: Tipping elements include Arctic sea ice, ice sheets and the Amazon rainforest.

q.s: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) was created following which conference?
q.x: The Stockholm Conference (1972) created UNEP.

q.s: Which of the following conferences is NOT correctly matched with its outcome?
